instructions: ANSWER QUESTION ONE AND ANY OTHER TWO QUESTIONS

parts.text: Define the following terms.
Algorithm
Tree
Binary tree
Linked list
Stack
Explain the four ways of representing an algorithm using suitable examples.
Using examples, explain the three types of proof and cite the situation where each can be used.
Write a C program to show the implementation of a stack.
Consider the directed graph with vertices v0 to v6 printed in the original paper.
In what order are the vertices visited for a depth-first search that starts at v0?
In what order are the vertices visited for a breadth-first search that starts at v0?
Draw a directed graph with five vertices and seven edges. Exactly one of the edges should be a loop, and do not have any multiple edges.
Explain how the breadth-first and depth-first searching algorithms function.
Using suitable examples, explain how the following graph traversing algorithms work: shortest paths, Euler and Hamilton cycles.
Explain the operations that can be done on each of the following data structure elements.
Queue operations
Stack operations
Tree operations
List operations
Given the following list of numbers 4, 6, 8, 12, 56, 23, 58, 19, show the operation of inserting the following numbers into the list at the specified position.
30 at position 8 in the list
10 at position 6 in the list
Suppose the above list was a queue, what would be the mode of operation for the above structure?
Show the algorithm for the above operations.
Explain the following terms.
Spanning tree
Asymptotic notation (the symbol is unreadable in the scan)
Preconditioning
i) What are the main differences between divide and conquer and dynamic programming? ii) What is the basic approach in solving a problem using dynamic programming?
Write down the characteristics of greedy algorithms.
